title: Unable to test a multipage app which consists a custom sidebar using AppTest
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I am facing an issue somewhat similar to [this](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8070), but during testing with AppTest. App functions as expected. Testing main.py works fine. Testing the page fails. 


### Reproducible Code Example

_No response_

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the following directory structure:

```
├── server
│   ├── main.py
│   ├── pages
│   │   └── register.py
│   └── utils.py
└── tests
    └── unit
        ├── test_main.py
        └── test_register.py
```
2. Disable sidebar in config.tom with 
```
[client]
showSidebarNavigation = false
```
3. Add your own custom sidebar in both main.py and register.py with the following two lines of code:
```
st.sidebar.page_link("main.py", label="Home")
st.sidebar.page_link("pages/register.py", label="Register")
```
4. Everything should work as expected when you run the app.
5. Write test for main in test_main.py
```
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath("server"))
def test_main_page():
    at = AppTest.from_file("server/main.py")
    at.run()
    assert not at.exception
```
6. Running the above test should pass.
7. Write a test for test_register.py as follows:
```
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath("server"))
def test_main_page():
    at = AppTest.from_file("server/pages/register.py")
    at.run()
    assert not at.exception
```

### Expected Behavior

The above test in test_register.py should pass.

### Current Behavior

streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException: Could not find page: `main.py`. Must be the file path relative to the main script, from the directory: `pages`. Only the main app file and files in the `pages/` directory are supported.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.32.2
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

If you are trying to test your main.ly page, why call AppTest on the registry.py page? The issue is that AppTest thinks registry.py _is_ the main app page here and is looking for pages relative to "that".

I see the problem though, You want to be able to run AppTest in a mode where it things the root of your directory is something other than the file being loaded. That may require an additional keyword argument...

I think you need to set up AppTest with main.py and then switch pages to registry.py with https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/9f9f03b8247897cdd334d972028a5bb1ea451046/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L381 If you want to test a subpage. 

[USER] I will note that the current docstring for AppTest claims that the capability provided by switch_page() doesn't exist 🫠. Perhaps that was an update that came later and we never removed the docstring note
[USER] Thank you. I got confused by the documentation. I thought switching page wasn't supported by AppTest. I will try this out.

Re-verified against current `develop` at `0aba4dab0b`.

Calling `AppTest.from_file("server/pages/register.py")` treats `register.py` as the main script, so `page_link("main.py")` is resolved relative to the `pages` directory. The supported multipage testing flow is to start from the actual main script and then switch pages:

```python
at = AppTest.from_file("server/main.py").run()
at.switch_page("pages/register.py").run()
assert not at.exception
```

That flow passes, and page switching has been supported since #8280. Closing as completed because the requested capability is implemented. The AppTest documentation can be clarified separately if the main-script requirement remains confusing.
